applicationContext: Synthetic engineering transfer application; not an official institutional prompt
prompt: Describe a technical project, your own role, a setback and what you learned.
requirements:
Describe your own role.
Describe a setback and your response.
Explain what you learned.
essay: Our robotics club wanted to sort paper cups by color. I wrote the sensor calibration routine while two teammates built the conveyor. Under the classroom lights the sensor misclassified blue cups as green. I compared readings with the lights on and off, covered the sensor with a cardboard hood, and tested the same twenty cups again. The hood reduced errors from eight cups to one. I recorded both trials so the next team could repeat the test. I learned to test the environment before assuming my code was wrong. On our next prototype I included lighting tests in the first checklist.

applicationContext: Synthetic business application; not an official institutional prompt
prompt: Describe a team contribution, its outcome and an ethical decision you faced.
requirements:
Describe your own contribution.
Describe the outcome.
Explain an ethical decision you personally faced.
essay: At our student shop I organized the weekly inventory sheet. I asked each volunteer to record deliveries in one shared spreadsheet instead of separate notebooks. I checked the entries against the boxes on Friday and taught the next shift how to find missing items. We stopped ordering products we already had and reduced duplicate orders during the next month. I learned to ask the people using a system what slows them down before designing a replacement.
activities: I also attended a school seminar about business ethics.

applicationContext: Synthetic personal statement; not an official institutional prompt
prompt: Describe a responsibility and how it changed your approach to supporting others.
requirements:
Describe your responsibility.
Explain a change in your approach.
essay: At the library I helped an older neighbor practice using the bus timetable app. On the first visit I tapped through every screen for him. The next week he could not repeat the steps alone. I asked him to hold the phone and tell me where he expected the next button to be. We wrote down the route together and practiced one change at a time. By the third visit he found his stop without my prompts. I learned that support should make room for another person to try, pause and choose. I now ask what someone wants to do before offering instructions.

prompt: Describe a project you led and explain what you learned from it.
requirements:
Describe the project you led in your essay.
Explain what you learned in your essay.
essay: I enjoy working with others and hope to learn more in college. I want to use my education to help people in my community.
activities: I led a neighborhood cleanup with six volunteers. I learned to check supplies before inviting people.
